conflicts.point: Whether mandatory pre-deployment mechanistic interpretability audits are necessary to prevent catastrophic model failures or primarily function as anti-competitive regulatory capture mechanisms.

positions.stance: Mandatory mechanistic interpretability audits and compute allocation rules are required because black-box runtime telemetry cannot detect latent internal risks before deployment.

Mandating internal interpretability audits creates regulatory barriers that impede market experimentation and technological progress, relying on speculative fears rather than empirical output metrics.
Mandated internal interpretability standards act as regulatory capture tools that protect incumbent firms while ignoring tangible, present-day environmental resource bottlenecks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether mandatory pre-deployment mechanistic interpretability audits are necessary to prevent catastrophic model failures or primarily function as anti-competitive regulatory capture mechanisms.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position correctly identifies a real epistemic gap in black-box testing, but the skeptic position correctly highlights immediate physical infrastructure limits and the anti-competitive risks of rigid mandates. Neither camp provides sufficient empirical evidence to prove that one concern outweighs the other at scale.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Data showing whether mandatory internal audits successfully prevent catastrophic AI failures without stifling startup formation would tip the balance.
